scenarios.name: nested-array-index
scenarios.why: Parsing and resolving multiple consecutive template brackets and chained index operator types. Rejected because the variable is called `grid`, which this engine registers as a type - "Illegal variable name". Nothing to do with nesting: the same script with the variable renamed to `matrix` compiles, indexing and all.

scenarios.name: nested-array-extract-row
scenarios.why: Inferring the inner element type of a nested template container when assigned to a separate variable.

scenarios.name: deep-nested-array
scenarios.why: Handling template recursion depth and lexing multiple closing angle brackets without ambiguity.

scenarios.name: dictionary-retrieve-value
scenarios.why: Resolving output reference parameters on non-generic dictionary access methods.

scenarios.name: nested-dictionary
scenarios.why: Tracking nested container value semantics when storing one dictionary instance inside another.

scenarios.name: array-of-dictionary
scenarios.why: Indexing an array instantiated with a non-primitive dictionary value type.

scenarios.name: class-array-member
scenarios.why: Resolving member access on a template container containing user class instances within a method.

scenarios.name: function-returns-array
scenarios.why: Propagating template container return types across function call expression boundaries.

scenarios.name: handle-assign-in-condition
scenarios.why: AngelScript treats assignments as statements rather than expressions, rejecting assignment inside conditions.

scenarios.name: value-assign-in-condition
scenarios.why: Assignments are strictly statements in AngelScript grammar and cannot be evaluated as condition expressions.

scenarios.name: handle-comparison-is
scenarios.why: Disambiguating handle identity comparison keywords from value equality operations.

scenarios.name: nested-array-method-condition
scenarios.why: Chaining multiple array index operators followed by member method invocation within a conditional expression. Rejected for the same reason as nested-array-index: the variable is named `grid`, a registered type. Not about the condition it was written for.

scenarios.name: class-op-equals-condition
scenarios.why: Resolving custom operator overload opEquals for equality expressions inside condition statements.

scenarios.name: handle-method-in-condition
scenarios.why: Resolving method calls via object handles used directly as boolean predicates in conditional expressions.

scenarios.name: triple-nested-loop-counters
scenarios.why: Tracking lexical scope chains and variable resolution across multiple nested for-loop headers.

scenarios.name: foreach-nested-array
scenarios.why: AngelScript does not support foreach syntax or range-based for loops, causing a syntax rejection.

scenarios.name: sibling-for-loops-same-counter
scenarios.why: Ensuring loop counter declarations in separate sibling scopes do not produce name collision errors.

scenarios.name: loop-variable-shadowing
scenarios.why: AngelScript strictly forbids shadowing any variable declared in an enclosing scope within the same function. A nested block is its own scope, so shadowing a loop counter inside the body is accepted - measured, and the same rule doc_p12 pins.

scenarios.name: nested-while-for-while-break
scenarios.why: Resolving loop control statements to the correct innermost loop construct across mixed loop types.

scenarios.name: loop-over-array-elements
scenarios.why: Dictionary key iteration typically requires an array of strings which depends on host type registrations, so a plain for loop over an array of ints is used instead.
